verdict.rationale: Buzz's core architecture is a Nostr WebSocket relay that agents connect to in real time — buzz-acp explicitly documents 'The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI,' and NOSTR.md documents a real-time wire protocol (NIP-29/NIP-42) any third-party client can connect to directly for group chat/reaction events. Agents get first-class identities (their own Nostr keypairs) and remote/headless agents operate entirely through relay-delivered messages/mentions per VISION_REMOTE_AGENTS.md, with a documented benchmark suite grading real-time reply/notification behavior. Missing for 10: no REST/OpenAPI events API (probes show openapi.json 404s), and no independent hands-on report confirming real-time reliability in production beyond first-party docs.
